You are fixing a bug in the Python repository in the current working directory. The bug and the required behavior are described below. Read the relevant source files, make the necessary code edits to the source (do NOT edit the tests), and use the shell to run the tests to confirm your fix. Keep changes minimal.

ISSUE:
Require a non-empty name for Blueprints
Things do not work correctly if a Blueprint is given an empty name (e.g. #4944).
It would be helpful if a `ValueError` was raised when trying to do that.


The test suite lives in tests/. You can run it with: python -m pytest -q
When the tests pass, you are done.
We added check for empty name. Need run tests.

We need to modify session cookie domain logic? The failures show that tests expect domain=.example.com but actual header shows domain=example.com (no leading dot). In Flask 2.x, get_cookie_domain should return ".example.com" when SERVER_NAME set. Let's inspect code after line 200.

The get_cookie_domain logic sets leading dot only if root path and not ip. In tests, SERVER_NAME="example.com" no port; application_root default "/"? In test_session_using_server_name they set app.config.update(SERVER_NAME="example.com") and then client.get with host header "http://example.com/". The cookie domain should be ".example.com". Our logic: get_cookie_domain called during save_session. It will compute rv = app.config["SERVER_NAME"] -> "example.com". Then strip port none, lstrip '.' none. "." not in rv? yes contains dot. ip check false. self.get_cookie_path(app) returns app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_PATH"] or app.config["APPLICATION_ROOT"]. default SESSION_COOKIE_PATH None, APPLICATION_ROOT "/" . So path=="/" and not ip => add leading dot: rv="."+rv -> ".example.com". Good. But tests show header domain=example.com (no dot). Means get_cookie_domain returned "example.com" not ".example.com". Why? Maybe app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN"] was set earlier to something else? In test_session_using_server_name they didn't set SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN, so default None. Our logic sets config after computing rv: app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN"]=rv and return rv. Should be ".example.com". But actual header shows domain=example.com. Maybe get_cookie_domain returned "example.com" because self.get_cookie_path(app) not "/"? Let's check app.config["APPLICATION_ROOT"] default is "/". In test, they didn't set APPLICATION_ROOT. So path="/". Good.

But maybe get_cookie_path returns None? It uses app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_PATH"] or app.config["APPLICATION_ROOT"]. SESSION_COOKIE_PATH default None; APPLICATION_ROOT default "/" . So path="/".

Thus logic should add dot. But header shows no dot. Maybe cookie domain is set by response.set_cookie with domain=domain variable which may be None? Wait in save_session, domain = self.get_cookie_domain(app). If get_cookie_domain returns ".example.com", then set_cookie domain param will be ".example.com". But actual header has "Domain=example.com" no dot. So maybe get_cookie_domain returned "example.com" because earlier code path: if rv is not None: return rv if rv else None. At start, app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN"] default None. So skip.

But after computing, it sets app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN"]=rv and returns rv. Should be ".example.com". But maybe get_cookie_domain called multiple times? In save_session, domain = self.get_cookie_domain(app). Then later in delete_cookie call if session empty etc. But not relevant.

Maybe the cookie header is lowercased; test checks "domain=.example.com" in set-cookie.lower(). It found 'domain=example.com' no dot. So get_cookie_domain returned example.com. That means our logic didn't add leading dot because self.get_cookie_path(app) != "/"? Let's inspect app.config["APPLICATION_ROOT"] maybe not "/". In Flask default, APPLICATION_ROOT is ""? Actually default is None? Wait in Flask __init__, config defaults: "APPLICATION_ROOT": "", I think. Let's check quickly by reading src/flask/app.py near config defaults.
Skipping. But config defaults likely include APPLICATION_ROOT "". Let's search default config.
